data.description:
## Description

**What**: Introduce merge.strategy and enforcement.strategy config keys; split merge-to-main.sh into a thin dispatcher that execs merge-to-main-direct.sh (extracted from current behavior) or merge-to-main-pr.sh (stub, implemented by S3a); update this project's dso-config.conf; audit all consumer references.
**Why**: This is the walking skeleton — the foundational change that makes all other epic stories possible without breaking existing behavior.
**Scope**:
- IN: Two new config keys with documented defaults; merge-to-main.sh becomes thin dispatcher; merge-to-main-direct.sh extracted from current merge-to-main.sh body; dso-config.conf update (merge.strategy=pr, enforcement.strategy=local); audit of consumer references (CLAUDE.md, WORKTREE-GUIDE.md, sprint/SKILL.md, end-session/SKILL.md, .claude/scripts/dso shim); --resume cross-strategy behavior defined; dispatcher fails loudly on unknown merge.strategy values
- OUT: PR-mode implementation (S3a/S3b); hook gating (S2); enforcement-gate library (S0.5)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, merge.strategy (direct|pr, default direct) and enforcement.strategy (local|ci|both, default local) config keys are readable via read-config.sh
  <- Satisfies: "Config keys merge.strategy (direct|pr, default direct) and enforcement.strategy (local|ci|both, default local) introduced"
- When this story is complete, merge-to-main.sh is a thin dispatcher that execs merge-to-main-direct.sh when merge.strategy=direct and stubs merge-to-main-pr.sh with a clear "not yet implemented" error when merge.strategy=pr
  <- Satisfies: "merge-to-main.sh becomes a thin dispatcher"
- When this story is complete, merge-to-main-direct.sh contains the extracted current behavior with no functional change; all existing merge-to-main tests pass
  <- Satisfies: "Direct-mode regression: merge-to-main.sh behaves identically to the pre-epic baseline"
- When this story is complete, this project's dso-config.conf is updated to merge.strategy=pr, enforcement.strategy=local
  <- Satisfies: "This project's dso-config.conf is updated within this epic to set merge.strategy=pr and enforcement.strategy=local"
- When this story is complete, CLAUDE.md, WORKTREE-GUIDE.md, sprint/SKILL.md, end-session/SKILL.md, and the .claude/scripts/dso shim are audited and continue to work correctly with the dispatcher pattern
  <- Satisfies: "merge-to-main.sh becomes a thin dispatcher"
- When this story is complete, merge-to-main.sh --resume is well-defined: PR-mode runs use a distinct state schema prefix; a direct-mode state file passed to a PR-mode --resume run is rejected with a clear error rather than silent corruption
  <- Satisfies: "Merge-to-main phases: sync → merge → version_bump → validate → push → archive → ci_trigger; state file"
- When this story is complete, dispatcher exits 1 with clear error on unknown merge.strategy values
  <- Satisfies: "merge-to-main.sh becomes a thin dispatcher"
- When this story is complete, CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md documents merge.strategy and enforcement.strategy keys with defaults, valid values, and behavior descriptions
  <- Satisfies: "Config keys merge.strategy and enforcement.strategy introduced"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Config key defaults must be documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md
- [Reliability] Dispatcher must handle SIGURG: state file must capture which sub-script was executing so --resume can route correctly

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a plugin maintainer, I can configure merge.strategy and enforcement.strategy and have merge-to-main.sh route to the correct merge implementation
